Every dollar wants to be in AI compute right now

ARK Invest's Brett Winton on why that's making Bitcoin's "insurance" more expensive to hold

"Right now the world is basically sending out this giant emergency spinning beacon. All capital available needs to go into AI compute infrastructure, because we need as much as possible."

"Any asset that's not generating immediate great returns looks net worse on that basis. And so the cost of holding Bitcoin for this insurance contract has gone up."

"It's not just a Bitcoin and cryptocurrency issue. That is an issue for all businesses of all stripes all over the world."

"There's a black hole, and there's kind of like the tidal force that's pulling money into creating the infrastructure we need for superintelligence."

"Given the prospective returns of building data centers, it's clear that there's not enough money in that pool. And so it means that there's still this call on capital from everywhere else."

"The tea-leaf readers whispering about a 'subdued' tone on the call are flatly wrong, in our opinion. This was one of the most unapologetically bullish Tesla calls in many a moon.

Think about it, on the call management said that:
• EVs have their highest backlog in 4 years, with Musk adding that "...we are producing and delivering as many cars as we can...".

i. Debt- $CRWV unsecured debt trading at 15%

b. AI native growth rates slowing
i. Anthropic revs 145% q/q in Q2 to 45% in Q3

ii. Openweight driving ASPs down ~50% since May

5) Datacenter moratoriums seem to be the only thing both parties agree on
a. This could get worse after the mid-terms with a less AI-friendly political climate

Some more thoughts:

1. In Texas, getting mineral rights waivers are harder and take longer than ever. Case law is useful but it’s even more critical than ever to have these in place especially in West Texas where there is lots of activity. 

2. East Texas is not buildable unless you’re a neocloud and can take the legal risk. Hyperscalers or foundational model companies may capitulate and come here but it will be a last resort type of thing. 

3. Power pipeline is clogged everywhere. Utilities are completely overwhelmed and will ratchet their pipelining process to flush out the squatters. This will mean higher capital commitments earlier in the process for those that are real. 

4.  Builders don’t have the economic authority to offer local incentives to get the utility to move them up in the queue. The ultimate offtaker isn’t as aggressive as they should be to accelerate grid connections. When the builder/offtaker is the same, these conditions get much better. This is a big benefit for being a well funded IG hyperscaler. 

5. Consumer pushback is still ratcheting up. Data centers are an easy target against the oligarchy who, collectively, still haven’t done enough to win society to their side.

en_summary: @scottmelker: A bank hack would be far worse than a crypto exchange hack. ARK Invest's Brett Winton says a bank hack could freeze the financial system, showing why holding Bitcoin could pay off. Explains differences in asset transfer and bearer instruments.
text:
A bank hack would be far worse than a crypto exchange hack.

ARK Invest's Brett Winton says a bank hack could freeze the financial system, showing why holding Bitcoin could pay off

"If a major crypto exchange got hacked in a profound way, literally the assets could be transferred onchain to somebody else, and then somebody else owns them. Big problem."

"On the other hand, it's kind of a simple problem. Somebody else has the private keys. These are effectively bearer instruments."

"If somebody goes into a bank, they wouldn't necessarily be able to take the money. But they could totally scramble the accounts of the bank in a way where it would actually be a much bigger problem for the financial system if we didn't know where the money was."

"Who owes money to who suddenly gets called into question, and it would totally freeze the local financial ecosystem, and depending on the size of the bank could severely arrest the global financial ecosystem."

"In those circumstances, if you have Bitcoin or any crypto asset that is digitally secured, you'd be like, well, at least I know I have this. I do think it's illustrative of the potential option value of the asset."

"If somebody goes into a bank, they wouldn't necessarily be able to take the money. But they could totally scramble the accounts of the bank in a way where it would actually be a much bigger problem for the financial system if we didn't know where the money was."

"Who owes money to who suddenly gets called into question, and it would totally freeze the local financial ecosystem, and depending on the size of the bank could severely arrest the global financial ecosystem."

zh_summary: @APompliano: his views: money printing means bitcoin, gold and land do well for 2 decades; AI is underestimated and top AI firms undervalued; bonds should not be considered by anyone under 50; venture and public markets blend within 5 years; rates and oil matter less today; and a Tesla SpaceX merger will create the largest company in history, never bet against Elon.

text:
My current views on investing:

- Government will never stop printing money, so bitcoin / gold / land will all do well for 2 decades

- AI is drastically underestimated and the best AI companies are significantly undervalued

- Shorting individual stocks is very difficult, so I wouldn’t try it but the biggest indicator of whether a company survives or not is the internal speed of iteration now 

- Bonds shouldn’t be in the conversation for anyone under age 50. Picking up pennies in front of steamroller 

- Venture investing & public markets will blend in next 5 years, so private valuations will rise due to lots more capital chasing a few great companies

- Young people should look at assets & markets that Wall Street hasn’t adopted yet. This used to be bitcoin/crypto, but now private markets, prediction markets, compute markets, and data brokering

- every investor should be sovereign. You can use a financial advisor, but you have to know your numbers, your strategy, and your risk exposure. AI makes this too easy (Silvia .com)

- Everyone arguing over interest rates, oil, and other historical macro factors are not wrong, but these just have less impact today (thx @jvisserlabs)

- agents are coming for finance and things are going to rapidly change. Don’t fight it, embrace it and use to your advantage.

- Tesla / SpaceX merger will happen and create largest company in human history. My simple rule is to never bet against Elon.

There are many more, but what are yours?
